clauses.reason: Section 1-101 (with the authority recital) continues the thirteen listed advisory committees until December 31, 1980. Executive Order 12258 of December 31, 1980, section 1-104, states that Executive Order No. 12110 is superseded, and section 1-105 states that the order is effective December 31, 1980; the order's own continuation date is also December 31, 1980, so the first end is 1980-12-31 (inclusive; exclusive reading 1980-12-30).

Section 1-102 assigns the functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for the listed committees to the head of the designated department or agency. It lasts as long as the continued committees and ends with the order. Executive Order 12258 of December 31, 1980, section 1-104, states that Executive Order No. 12110 is superseded, and section 1-105 states that the order is effective December 31, 1980; the order's own continuation date is also December 31, 1980, so the first end is 1980-12-31 (inclusive; exclusive reading 1980-12-30).

Section 1-103 revokes Executive Orders No. 11482, 11849, 11534, 11971, 11973 and 11998, which established committees that had terminated or whose work was completed. A revocation is performed once it takes effect; the order became effective December 31, 1978 (section 1-105), so this command was exhausted on 1978-12-31. The revocations themselves are the surviving consequence and are not affected by the later supersession of this order.

Section 1-104 supersedes Executive Order No. 11948. It was performed when the order took effect on December 31, 1978 (section 1-105), the same day on which section 1 of Executive Order 11948 ran out by its own terms; the supersession of EO 11948 is the surviving consequence.
Section 1-105 fixes the effective date of the order as December 31, 1978. It is a commencement provision spent when the order took effect on 1978-12-31.

research_rationale:
EO 12110 (signed 1978-12-28), Continuance of Certain Federal Advisory Committees, continues thirteen committees until December 31, 1980 (1-101), assigns functions (1-102), revokes six orders (1-103), supersedes EO 11948 (1-104) and sets its effective date, December 31, 1978 (1-105). The held Federal Register text was read in full and the inventory corrected to those sections. EO 12258 (1980-12-31) supersedes EO 12110 in its section 1-104, effective December 31, 1980, which is also the order's own end date; the whole-order end is 1980-12-31. Sections 1-103 to 1-105 were performed on taking effect 1978-12-31. A held-text search by number for the committee-establishing orders listed in 1-101 found EO 12258 (continuation), EO 12299 (revokes EO 11970 and 12258 section 1-101(f)), EO 12131 (revokes 11753) and EO 12196 (revokes 11807); each of those revokes an establishing order after 1978 and none supersedes or amends EO 12110, so none ends a clause of this order earlier.

savings.reason: The committees' establishing orders are independent instruments, and Executive Order 12258 continues many of them until December 31, 1982 under its own section 1-101; they do not depend on this order after 1980-12-31. The six orders revoked by 1-103 stay revoked.
